context.purpose: Publish bounded PNG frame sequences or declared Aseprite sprite sheets as verified H.264 or FFV1 videos. The editable starting example is plan-only until its absolute PNG path is replaced. An optional deliverable policy expresses dimensions, frame count, duration, file size and decoded pixel-error requirements.
context.assumptions: Exactly one node; explicit input order and constant frame rate. A matching ffprobe executable is required beside FFmpeg. The adaptor uses their public command-line interfaces.
context.constraints: No audio, arbitrary filter graph or colour-management guarantee. PNG subset and byte/frame limits apply; alpha composites onto black. H.264 needs even dimensions and is lossy. Sheet durations must be representable at the chosen frame rate.
context.inspection: Inspect video and retained native decode/probe evidence. Verify dimensions, frame count, rate and duration, and every decoded frame. FFV1 must match RGB bytes; H.264 mean RGB error is bounded at 16/255 per frame. These are bounded fidelity checks, not perceptual certification. Deliverable acceptance is independently reconstructed from authored requirements and actual retained native observations.
context.recovery: INVALID_RESOURCE requires absolute PNG/metadata paths. Missing inputs need actual files, not placeholder paths. Correct dimensions or frame timing for native rejection; use FFV1 if H.264 exceeds the fidelity bound. Replan and rerun with retained failure logs. DELIVERABLE_NOT_MET retains a correct video with observed requirements and corrective next actions; revise sources, fps or codec before a fresh run.

workflow.scope: Consumes image, spriteSheet and spriteMetadata artifacts. Explicit frame order, fixed rate, alpha-on-black and codec-dependent losses; no automatic format conversion.

composition.scope: Shared document references, pure value functions and expressions resolve for every finite analytic visit before native validation.

lifecycle.timeout: Native encoding and decoding use a shared elapsed-time budget.
lifecycle.cancellation: Owned native subprocess trees use shared cancellation and retain partial evidence.
lifecycle.logs: Retain stage stdout/stderr, commands, probe output, decoded RGB and submissions.
lifecycle.verification: Recheck full decoded RGB against retained inputs, dimensions, count, duration, hashes and declared codec-dependent error limits. Authored deliverable acceptance is reconstructed from native duration, dimensions/count, actual compressed byte size and per-frame mean RGB errors; unmet results cannot be published as successes. New native decode/probe launchers bind the encoded input digest to each owned stage; launcher source, bindings and decoded/probe output digests are replayed offline. Historical direct commands remain explicitly unbound. Source capture and scheduler fingerprints reject non-regular inputs before opening and recheck descriptors, with bounded byte reads.

data.scope: Equal dimensions and bounded non-interlaced PNG subset.

losses: Frame duration must be representable at the chosen constant fps.
H.264 is lossy; FFV1 is byte-exact after alpha compositing.

inspection.scope: Inspect retained probe and verification JSON.
inspection.limits: Video playback is external; the shared console does not advertise a video player.

authoring.reuse: Bind ordered PNG files, choose the declared codec and change fps with a JSON pointer edit. Plan the new revision and verify a fresh run; the acceptance cases supply portable repository fixture bindings.

workflow.scope: Declared artifact receipts, scheduler provenance and explicit handoffs; verify each consumer format.

native-inspection.scope: Inspect retained publications and receipts; no native node inspection hook is advertised.

composition.scope: Shared document references, pure value functions and expressions resolve for every finite analytic visit before native validation.

mpi.scope: Only serial execution is qualified; do not request multiple ranks.

reusable-inputs.scope: The registered hook hashes external inputs for scheduler reuse.

time-batches.scope: No finite native time-list batching support in this route.

source-authoring.scope: Edit ordinary JSON through the shared draft source; planning checks the current revision.

property-authoring.scope: Use atomic JSON pointer patches through the shared draft model; node commands apply only to node-shaped routes.

live-editing.scope: Use bounded batch execution; no persistent native editing session is promised.

native-save.scope: Inspect and reuse declared publications; no console native-save extension is advertised for this route.

conversion.scope: Explicit PNG or sprite-sheet to video encoding; FFV1 preserves RGB after alpha-on-black compositing, H.264 is lossy. No automatic conversion planning.

cases.scope: One known PNG encoded as FFV1 at 25 fps; independently decoded RGB must be byte-exact after alpha compositing. Does not qualify H.264 or sprite timing.
